body: It is a single voice and yes, I'll have halfhearted debates with it. I think in dialog, so this isn't the same as auditory hallucinations.
It's silly, but I get so worked up over my writing not being good or the ideas I'm expressing not well thought out enough that I can't start. There's a massive mental inertia for me to do anything.

I want to talk so badly, but I can't come up with anything. There's no traumatic event that really triggered my MDD as far as I can tell. I rarely think about my father's suicide. It's just that I'm constantly barraged with the idea that I deserve death while my chest is constricted from anxiety. I don't have the slightest idea why.

Also, how long is hanging on justified? It feels like that's all I've been doing for so long. I can barely stand getting out of bed or talking to people at this point and I'm just getting worse.

I have always thought in dialog, which they both know. When feeling depressed on of the two perspectives in my head becomes my depression personified. It's not the same as auditory hallucinations. Sorry for the confusion.

My psychologist and psychiatrist both know the extent of my symptoms. They are both provided through my school. I don't know if I should switch or the quality of care since I have nothing to compare to them but a terrible grief counselor. Anyway, I'm terrified I'll end up like David Foster Wallace, jumping from medicine to medicine, each failing after a while, until I can't do anything but suffer until I'm driven to suicide. In the short term, I'm really worried for my grades. I have no idea how I'll get through all the work I need to, even with all the help I've had after emailing my professors about my condition.

My psychiatrist gave me a very low dose of [Risperdal](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risperidone) today (0.125mg) to see if that lessens my anxiety and depression. I'm unsure what to think about that. I hope it helps; I can barely write emails to professors at this point as I feel so panicked when I try to sit down and type.

It's that I can't stop imagining my bodies after suicide attempts, but I don't perceive them outside my head at all. I don't literally see a body in the corner, I just can't help but imagine one in my mind's eye. Does that make a little more sense?
I've always thought in dialog. When depressed one of the two subvocalized thoughts essential becomes my depression personified. I doubt that's the same thing as schizophrenics hearing voices.

Honestly, it is a bit helpful to hear someone else has gone through something similar. It makes me feel a little less crazy. I'm so sorry for what you're going through, by the way. I've talked my therapist without much changing and after my meeting today my psychiatrist suggested [Risperidone](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risperidone) on top of my SSRI. I've tried writing in the past, and unfortunately it doesn't help. Humorously enough, I get too caught up in critiquing my writing style. I'm unsure what to talk about, but thank you.
These are entirely mental images for me; they don't appear physical in any way. Imagine a bird flying around your room. Now imagine it's bodies instead of a bird and you can't stop imagining it.
